log.text: Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Incineroar

decisions.rationale: Lead Whimsicott and Gholdengo for immediate priority Tailwind, Helping Hand pressure, and Make It Rain while Good as Gold blocks Parting Shot. Mega Blastoise gives strong Water Pulse and Aura Sphere coverage into Incineroar and Kingambit, while Tauros adds Intimidate, Close Combat, and Rock Slide pressure against the opposing Fire and Steel threats.
decisions.notebook: Preferred core is Whimsicott + Gholdengo, using priority Tailwind or Helping Hand with Gholdengo's spread pressure; Good as Gold is valuable into Incineroar's Parting Shot. Mega Blastoise is the main answer to Incineroar and Kingambit, while Tauros-Blaze supplies Intimidate, Close Combat, and Rock Slide coverage. Ninetales-A can instead support a snow/Aurora Veil mode when durability is more important; Maushold offers Follow Me redirection.

decisions.rationale: Incineroar+Talonflame lead: Fake Out disrupts Whimsicott Tailwind, Gale Wings Tailwind secures speed, double Fire threatens Whimsicott/Gholdengo/Ninetales. Gardevoir Mega Hyper Voice nukes through Maushold Friend Guard and handles Tauros; Kingambit Kowtow Cleave OHKOes Gholdengo and Iron Head 4x destroys Ninetales-A. Passho Berry Incineroar pivots safely vs Blastoise.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead: Incineroar+Talonflame, back Gardevoir+Kingambit. Triple Fire (Incineroar Flare Blitz, Talonflame Flare Blitz/Brave Bird, Gardevoir Mystical Fire) torches Whimsicott, Gholdengo, Ninetales-A. Kingambit Kowtow Cleave for Gholdengo, Iron Head 4x into Ninetales-A. Incineroar Passho Berry survives Mega Blastoise Water Pulse. Talonflame Gale Wings Tailwind for speed control. Gardevoir Mega Pixilate Hyper Voice as spread nuke.

decisions.rationale: Tailwind establishes speed control for Gholdengo and the backline, while Power Gem cleanly OHKOs Talonflame through its 4x weakness. This also removes Gale Wings and opposing Tailwind pressure; even if Incineroar uses Fake Out, Gholdengo still secures the knockout.
decisions.notebook: Whimsicott + Gholdengo remains the preferred opening core. Power Gem is a guaranteed OHKO on Talonflame from full HP with the current Gholdengo build. Mega Blastoise is the main answer to Incineroar and Kingambit; Tauros-Paldea-Blaze provides Intimidate, Close Combat, and Rock Slide coverage. Ninetales-A supports a snow/Aurora Veil mode, while Maushold offers Follow Me redirection.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out (+3) flinches Whimsicott before its Prankster Tailwind/Encore. Talonflame Tailwind (+1 Gale Wings) resolves before Gholdengo attacks, securing speed control even if Power Gem OHKOs Talonflame afterward. If Gholdengo Make It Rain instead, Talonflame lives comfortably (33-48%). Worst case: Helping Hand + Power Gem still only trades Talonflame for our permanent Tailwind.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead: Incineroar+Talonflame, back Gardevoir+Kingambit. Triple Fire (Incineroar Flare Blitz, Talonflame Flare Blitz/Brave Bird, Gardevoir Mystical Fire) torches Whimsicott, Gholdengo, Ninetales-A. Kingambit Kowtow Cleave for Gholdengo, Iron Head 4x into Ninetales-A. Incineroar Passho Berry survives Mega Blastoise Water Pulse. Talonflame Gale Wings Tailwind for speed control. Gardevoir Mega Pixilate Hyper Voice as spread nuke. Gholdengo Power Gem OHKOs Talonflame — must respect. Whimsicott Helping Hand (+6 with Prankster) outruns Fake Out (+3) but Tailwind more likely. Prankster fails vs Dark-type targets; Incineroar immune to Encore.

decisions.rationale: Kingambit resists both Gholdengo STABs (MakeItRain 0.5x, ShadowBall 0.5x) while threatening 2x KowtowCleave. Gardevoir is weak to Steel/Ghost and HyperVoice hits neutral into Whimsicott + NVE into Gholdengo. Incineroar stays in to FlareBlitz Whimsicott (2x, breaks Sash). Whimsicott almost certainly Prankster Tailwinds this turn, but Kingambit's bulk absorbs the follow-up safely.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Triple Fire lead (Incineroar+Talonflame) torched Whimsicott/Gholdengo/Ninetales-A. Talonflame fainted turn 1 to Gholdengo PowerGem after setting Tailwind. Kingambit now replaces Talonflame — its Dark/Steel typing walls Gholdengo's dual STAB and KowtowCleave threatens 2x. Gardevoir+Mega held in back for later; Pixilate HyperVoice as spread nuke but poor into Steel-heavy board. Incineroar PasshoBerry survives Mega Blastoise WaterPulse. Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind expected; Encore/HelpingHand fail vs Dark Incineroar. Opponent has 2 unrevealed (Blastoise, Maushold, Tauros-Blaze, Ninetales-A); only 2 of these in game.

decisions.rationale: Encore Incineroar’s previously used Fake Out, forcing a wasted move if it remains in. Protect preserves Gholdengo from Kingambit’s super-effective Dark pressure while avoiding a risky low-confidence attack into Passho Incineroar; Whimsicott can support the core next turn.
decisions.notebook: Whimsicott + Gholdengo remains the preferred opening core. Mega Blastoise is the main answer to Incineroar and Kingambit; Tauros-Paldea-Blaze provides Intimidate, Close Combat, and Rock Slide coverage. Ninetales-A supports a snow/Aurora Veil mode, while Maushold offers Follow Me redirection. Preserve Gholdengo against Dark priority when possible and use Whimsicott’s Prankster utility to control tempo.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind is unstoppable (+1 prio vs our Dark types). Gholdengo is the real threat; doubling it with Flare Blitz (64.9-116%) + Kowtow Cleave (83.5-151.9%) virtually guarantees the KO before it can attack. Even if Gholdengo Protects, we lose little—both our mons stay healthy and our Tailwind outlasts theirs. Good as Gold blocks Parting Shot, so pivot plays are off the table.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Talonflame fainted T1 after setting Tailwind. Kingambit in back with Supreme Overlord (1 fallen). Opponent brought 4: Whimsicott/Gholdengo confirmed; 2 of Blastoise/Maushold/Tauros-Blaze/Ninetales-A unrevealed. Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind expected every few turns; Encore/HelpingHand fail vs Dark types. Gholdengo Good as Gold blocks all status moves including Parting Shot. Incineroar PasshoBerry survives Mega Blastoise Water Pulse. Gardevoir+Mega in back as spread nuke but weak to Steel. Opponent likely to set their own Tailwind T2; we maintain speed parity after.

decisions.rationale: Double-switch into the intended Incineroar/Kingambit answers: Blastoise takes the slot currently occupied by Whimsicott, while Tauros preserves Gholdengo from Dark pressure and supplies Intimidate against Kingambit. This also sets up a safer Mega Blastoise turn with both offensive options retained.
decisions.notebook: Whimsicott + Gholdengo remains a preferred opening, but preserve Gholdengo against Dark attacks and priority. Mega Blastoise is the primary Incineroar/Kingambit answer; Tauros-Paldea-Blaze is valuable for Intimidate, Close Combat, and Rock Slide. Opponent has revealed Incineroar, Kingambit, and fainted Talonflame; one unrevealed slot remains among Gardevoir, Serperior, and Dragapult.

decisions.rationale: Both our mons outspeed both foes under Tailwind. Double-target Gholdengo: Flare Blitz (59-130%) + Kowtow Cleave (77-167%) almost certainly KOs through anything but a lucky reduced-rate Protect. Whimsicott's Prankster status moves fail vs our Dark types, so it can't set Tailwind or Encore us; Moonblast does negligible damage. Removing Gholdengo leaves Whimsicott helpless, and we maintain board control with Gardevoir in back.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Talonflame fainted T1 after setting Tailwind. Kingambit Supreme Overlord (1 fallen). Opponent brought 4: Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Prankster)/Gholdengo (Wise Glasses, Good as Gold) confirmed; 2 of Blastoise/Maushold/Tauros-Blaze/Ninetales-A unrevealed. Key: Whimsicott Prankster status moves fail vs Dark types (Incineroar/Kingambit). Gholdengo Protect success rate reduced after T2 use. Gardevoir-Mega in back as potential spread cleaner with Pixilate Hyper Voice. Incineroar holds Passho Berry for Mega Blastoise Water Pulse. Opponent likely to bring Fighting coverage (Tauros or Blastoise Aura Sphere) threatening Kingambit's 4x weakness.

decisions.rationale: Mega Water Pulse pressures Incineroar through its Passho Berry while Close Combat guarantees the Kingambit KO, preventing its priority from controlling the endgame. This trades favorably even if Kingambit uses Sucker Punch, and preserves the option to use Blastoise as the primary answer to the remaining Fire/Dark threats.
decisions.notebook: Whimsicott + Gholdengo remains a preferred opening. Preserve Gholdengo from Dark attacks and priority when possible. Mega Blastoise is the primary answer to Incineroar and Kingambit; Tauros-Paldea-Blaze is valuable for Intimidate, Close Combat, and Rock Slide. Opponent's fourth Pokémon is one of Gardevoir, Serperior, or Dragapult; scout its identity and set before committing future positioning.

decisions.rationale: Kingambit faces guaranteed OHKO from Tauros Close Combat and possible OHKO from Blastoise Aura Sphere; Protect is essential. Incineroar outspeeds both foes under Tailwind and Parting Shots Blastoise to lower its SpA before pivoting to Gardevoir. Even if they double-target Incineroar's slot, Gardevoir comfortably survives the combined hits (43–64%). Next turn Gardevoir Mega Evolves with Tailwind up for Pixilate Hyper Voice pressure.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Talonflame fainted T1. Kingambit Supreme Overlord (1 fallen). Opponent brought Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Prankster), Gholdengo (Wise Glasses, Good as Gold), Blastoise (Blastoisinite), Tauros-Paldea-Blaze (Black Belt, Intimidate). Whimsicott Prankster status moves fail vs Dark types. Gholdengo Protect success rate decays. Incineroar holds Passho Berry for Mega Blastoise Water Pulse. Gardevoir-Mega is key spread cleaner with Pixilate Hyper Voice; preserve it. Tauros 4x Fighting threatens Kingambit; Blastoise Aura Sphere also 4x. Parting Shot pivots are crucial for momentum.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Tauros's Close Combat guarantees the Kingambit KO, while Blastoise targets Gardevoir rather than redundantly attacking a likely Protect target. This also pressures both foes if Kingambit's weakened Protect succeeds.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's fourth Pokémon in game 1 was Gardevoir, which revealed Mega Launcher before any Mega Evolution confirmation. Continue scouting the opponent's remaining roster and preserve Gholdengo from Dark attacks and priority when possible. Mega Blastoise remains the primary answer to Incineroar and Kingambit; Tauros-Paldea-Blaze remains valuable for Intimidate, Close Combat, and Rock Slide.

decisions.rationale: Switch to Gholdengo: it is immune to Gardevoir's Hyper Voice and preserves Whimsicott's Prankster utility for a later turn, while Blastoise remains the key answer to Incineroar and Kingambit. Though Incineroar threatens with Darkest Lariat, this is preferable to exposing Whimsicott to likely immediate attacks.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has revealed Incineroar, Kingambit, Mega Gardevoir, and Talonflame in game 1; Serperior and Dragapult were not brought. Mega Gardevoir revealed Mega Launcher before evolving. Preserve Gholdengo from Dark attacks and priority when possible; Mega Blastoise is the primary answer to Incineroar and Kingambit. Tauros remains a useful Intimidate/Close Combat/Rock Slide option when available.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolve Gardevoir for Pixilate Hyper Voice: 35-97% to 57% Tauros (~50% KO chance) + 25-63% to Blastoise. Switch Kingambit→Incineroar to dodge Tauros's guaranteed Close Combat OHKO. Incineroar Intimidate stacks on both foes; may survive even a double-target. Kingambit preserved for late-game Supreme Overlord cleanup with Gardevoir-Mega.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Talonflame fainted T1. Gardevoir-Mega is primary win condition with Pixilate Hyper Voice (167 Spe Timid). Kingambit Supreme Overlord stacking (1 fallen so far). Incineroar holds Passho Berry for Blastoise-Mega Water Pulse. Opponent: Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Prankster—status fails vs Dark), Gholdengo (Wise Glasses, Good as Gold), Blastoise-Mega (Mega Launcher), Tauros-Paldea-Blaze (Black Belt, Intimidate). Tauros 4x Fighting and Blastoise Aura Sphere both OHKO-threaten Kingambit. Parting Shot pivots are critical. Preserve Gardevoir-Mega; Kingambit gains value as allies fall.

decisions.rationale: Make It Rain guarantees the KO on Mega Gardevoir despite spread reduction, while also chipping Incineroar. Water Pulse targets Incineroar, the primary remaining threat and Blastoise’s best matchup; preserving Blastoise with Protect would surrender valuable damage.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s revealed team for this game includes Incineroar, Kingambit, Mega Gardevoir, and Talonflame; Serperior and Dragapult were not brought. Preserve Gholdengo from Dark attacks and priority when possible. Mega Blastoise is the primary answer to Incineroar and Kingambit. Tauros is unavailable after fainting, so Whimsicott remains the only reserve and should be used for Prankster support or Tailwind when appropriate. Mega Gardevoir’s Speed is uncertain and may move before Gholdengo.

decisions.rationale: Gardevoir Protects to dodge Gholdengo's threatening Make It Rain/Shadow Ball (81-118% OHKO range). Incineroar Parting Shots Blastoise to -3 Atk/-2 SpA, then pivots to Kingambit who walls Gholdengo's STABs and brings Supreme Overlord pressure. Blastoise at -1 SpA can't threaten Incineroar meaningfully even with Power Gem+Aura Sphere combined (max ~88%). Next turn Gardevoir+Kingambit dominate the crippled board.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Talonflame fainted T1. Gardevoir-Mega Timid 167 Spe Pixilate Hyper Voice is primary win condition. Kingambit Supreme Overlord (1 fallen). Incineroar holds Passho Berry, Careful nature. Opponent: Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Prankster—status fails vs Dark types), Gholdengo (Wise Glasses, Good as Gold—immune to status moves including Parting Shot), Blastoise-Mega (Mega Launcher), Tauros-Paldea-Blaze (fainted). Key: Gholdengo Make It Rain OHKO-threatens Gardevoir; must Protect or KO Gholdengo first. Kingambit resists both Gholdengo STABs. Parting Shot cycling preserves Incineroar for Intimidate re-use. Whimsicott Encore is blocked by Dark types.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Aura Sphere pressures Kingambit for a possible KO while avoiding its poor matchup into Gardevoir. Gholdengo Protect blocks Kingambit’s Dark priority and buys safety from Gardevoir’s attacks, preserving it for the following turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 revealed the opponent brought Incineroar, Kingambit, Mega Gardevoir, and Talonflame; Serperior and Dragapult were not brought. Preserve Gholdengo from Dark attacks and priority when possible. Mega Blastoise is the primary answer to Incineroar and Kingambit. Whimsicott is the only reserve and should provide Prankster support or Tailwind when appropriate.

decisions.rationale: Hyper Voice damages both foes (Blastoise 31-55%, Gholdengo 17-32%) while Kowtow Cleave guarantees Gholdengo KO (83-151% + Hyper Voice chip = 100% min). Gholdengo moves before Kingambit but after Gardevoir; Gardevoir may take Shadow Ball (36-53%) + Water Pulse (12-19%) = 49-72% from 65% HP — survives most rolls. Even if Gardevoir faints, Incineroar + Kingambit clean Blastoise 2v1.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Talonflame fainted T1. Gardevoir-Mega Timid 167 Spe Pixilate Hyper Voice primary win condition. Kingambit Supreme Overlord (1 fallen) with Black Glasses. Incineroar Careful, Passho Berry consumed. Opponent: Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Prankster—status fails vs Dark), Gholdengo (Wise Glasses, Good as Gold), Blastoise-Mega (Mega Launcher, -3 Atk/-2 SpA), Tauros-Paldea-Blaze (fainted). Gholdengo -2 SpA from Make It Rain. Kingambit Kowtow Cleave OHKO-threatens Gholdengo. Gardevoir Protect success rate reduced after T6 use. Key: remove Gholdengo to enable Hyper Voice spam; Kingambit resists both Gholdengo STABs.

decisions.rationale: Aura Sphere guarantees the KO on Kingambit before it can use Sucker Punch. Shadow Ball heavily damages Gardevoir while Hyper Voice is ineffective against Gholdengo, preserving offensive pressure and removing the immediate priority threat.
decisions.notebook: Opponent brought Incineroar, Kingambit, Mega Gardevoir, and Talonflame; Serperior and Dragapult were not brought in Game 1. Preserve Gholdengo from Dark attacks and priority when possible. Mega Blastoise is the primary answer to Incineroar and Kingambit; Whimsicott is the reserve support option.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Hyper Voice guaranteed KOs Blastoise (31.2% min > 22% HP) before it can Aura Sphere Kingambit. Kingambit Protects to dodge Gholdengo's Make It Rain (10.6-15.1% = KO at 8% HP). Gardevoir survives any single -2 SpA hit (Shadow Ball max 53.1%, Make It Rain max 58.5%). Next turn: both alive vs Gholdengo + Whimsicott, Kingambit Sucker Punch threatens Gholdengo.

Incineroar Careful 50% HP, Passho Berry consumed. Opponent: Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Prankster), Gholdengo (Wise Glasses, Good as Gold, -2 SpA), Blastoise-Mega (Mega Launcher, -3 Atk/-2 SpA, 22% HP), Tauros-Paldea-Blaze (fainted). Gholdengo Protect success rate reduced. Kingambit Kowtow Cleave/Sucker Punch OHKO-threatens Gholdengo. Gardevoir Hyper Voice KOs Blastoise from 22%. Key: eliminate Gholdengo to enable Hyper Voice spam.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott’s Prankster Encore acts first and locks Gardevoir-Mega into its previously used Hyper Voice, which cannot affect Gholdengo. Gholdengo then uses super-effective Shadow Ball, guaranteeing the KO from 15%, while avoiding the risk of Mystical Fire.
decisions.notebook: Opponent brought Incineroar, Kingambit, Mega Gardevoir, and Talonflame in Game 1; Serperior and Dragapult were not brought. Preserve Gholdengo from Dark attacks and priority when possible. Mega Blastoise is the primary answer to Incineroar and Kingambit; Whimsicott is the reserve support option.

decisions.rationale: Protect (+4) outruns Prankster Encore (+1), blocking Gholdengo's Shadow Ball while Sucker Punch strikes first. If Whimsicott Encores, Gardevoir is locked into Hyper Voice for next turn but survives. Sucker Punch (62.9-138.3%) into 71% Gholdengo likely KOs; even on a low roll, Hyper Voice next turn finishes it. This handles Encore, Tailwind, Helping Hand, and double-attack lines safely.

Incineroar Careful 50% HP, Passho Berry consumed. Opponent: Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Prankster), Gholdengo (Wise Glasses, Good as Gold, -2 SpA), Blastoise-Mega (fainted), Tauros-Paldea-Blaze (fainted). Gholdengo Protect used 3x (success rate ~12.5%). Kingambit Protect used last turn (success rate reduced). Gardevoir Protect used 1x (normal rate). Whimsicott Encore cannot target Dark-type Kingambit. Sucker Punch + Hyper Voice combined minimum 78.4% > 71% Gholdengo HP.

decisions.rationale: Moonblast targets Kingambit for a super-effective hit and should secure the KO at 7% HP, removing its priority threat. Gardevoir is already locked into Protect by Encore, so it cannot meaningfully interfere this turn.

Whimsicott at 86% HP means Focus Sash is inactive. Hyper Voice (45.5-89.6%) + Iron Head (80.2-155.6%) combined minimum 125.7% > 86%, always KO. Even if Whimsicott is faster and Moonblasts one attacker first, the survivor's move KOs Whimsicott same turn—game over since it's their last Pokémon.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Won by cleaning last foe with Hyper Voice + Iron Head. Whimsicott Focus Sash was offline at 86% HP. Series now 1-0. Opponent team: Whimsicott (Prankster Sash), Gholdengo (Good as Gold Wise Glasses), Blastoise-Mega, Tauros-Paldea-Blaze. Key lessons: Gardevoir-Mega Pixilate Hyper Voice is primary win condition; Kingambit Supreme Overlord Black Glasses cleans late-game; Incineroar Fake Out resets on switch. Whimsicott Encore cannot target Dark types.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.
Moonblast into Mega Gardevoir moves before its revealed Speed range and guarantees the KO from 15%; targeting Incineroar cannot KO. Gholdengo has no active action.

Preserve Gholdengo from Dark attacks and priority whenever possible. Mega Blastoise is the primary answer to Incineroar and Kingambit; Whimsicott is the reserve support option.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out (+3 priority) outspeeds everything Whimsicott can do. Hyper Voice is a guaranteed KO from 1% HP (no Sash at 1%). Whimsicott flinches and can't act. Clean win.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 won. Series 1-0. Opponent team: Whimsicott (Prankster Sash), Gholdengo (Good as Gold Wise Glasses), Blastoise-Mega, Tauros-Paldea-Blaze. Gardevoir-Mega Pixilate Hyper Voice is primary win condition; Kingambit Supreme Overlord Black Glasses cleans late-game; Incineroar Fake Out resets on switch. Whimsicott Encore cannot target Dark types. Focus Sash only protects from full HP.

reflections.summary: Lost mainly because the team-preview plan was unfavorable: Whimsicott was vulnerable to Incineroar’s Fake Out, the opponent established Tailwind, and Mega Blastoise was too slow and repeatedly weakened by Mega Gardevoir’s Hyper Voice and Parting Shot. Tauros added little, while Gholdengo was eventually exposed to Kingambit’s Sucker Punch. Mega Blastoise was a reasonable Incineroar/Kingambit answer but did not suit the opponent’s strong spread-damage mode by itself.
reflections.adjustment: Bring Dragapult over Tauros to apply immediate pressure to Mega Gardevoir and Talonflame, rather than relying on Whimsicott to establish speed control into Fake Out and opposing Tailwind. Keep Gholdengo protected from Kingambit’s Dark attacks and priority, and use Mega Blastoise after Gardevoir is pressured.
reflections.notebook: Opponent favors Incineroar Fake Out plus Parting Shot cycling, Mega Gardevoir Protect and repeated Hyper Voice, and Talonflame Tailwind. Kingambit has Protect and Sucker Punch, so Gholdengo must not be left exposed to it. Do not rely on Whimsicott as the sole speed-control plan into Incineroar/Talonflame. Prefer bringing Dragapult for immediate pressure on Mega Gardevoir and Talonflame; Mega Blastoise is useful into Incineroar and Kingambit but is vulnerable to Gardevoir’s spread damage and stat drops.

reflections.summary: We won because we successfully cycled Incineroar's Parting Shot to repeatedly debuff Blastoise-Mega, while Gardevoir-Mega's Pixilate Hyper Voice spread damage through their team. The opponent's early double Protect gave us a free switch into Gardevoir, and Kingambit's Sucker Punch cleaned Gholdengo. Their Tauros was neutralized by Intimidate and Hyper Voice, and Whimsicott's Encore was useless against our Dark types.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, consider leading Incineroar + Gardevoir to avoid Talonflame being sniped by Gholdengo's Power Gem again. Use Icy Wind for speed control if Tailwind is not safe. Alternatively, replace Talonflame with a different support if Gholdengo is brought.
reflections.notebook: Game 1 won. Series 1-0. Opponent team: Whimsicott (Prankster Focus Sash, Encore/Moonblast), Gholdengo (Good as Gold Wise Glasses, Make It Rain/Shadow Ball/Power Gem/Protect), Blastoise-Mega (Water Pulse/Aura Sphere/Ice Beam/Protect), Tauros-Paldea-Blaze (Intimidate Black Belt, Close Combat/Raging Bull/Rock Slide/Protect). Maushold (Friend Guard Follow Me) and Ninetales-Alola (Snow Warning Aurora Veil) not brought. Opponent led Whimsicott + Gholdengo, used double Protect turn 2, then pivoted to Blastoise + Tauros for double Intimidate. Gholdengo's Power Gem threatens Talonflame. Blastoise's Aura Sphere threatens Kingambit. Whimsicott's Encore fails on Dark types. Focus Sash guarantees survival at full HP. Future: expect possible Maushold redirection or Ninetales Aurora Veil. Gardevoir-Mega Hyper Voice is primary win condition; Kingambit cleans late but is frail to Fairy. Incineroar's Parting Shot cycling is key for debuffing. Consider Icy Wind for speed control if Talonflame is risky.
